ready1_open_rewrite.raw_question_text:
A washing machine spin dryer rotates about a vertical axis. When operating at a steady state, its rotational speed is $\mathfrak{n}=600\mathrm{r/min}$ (i.e., 600 revolutions per minute). The spin dryer accelerates from rest to its steady-state rotational speed in a time interval of $\mathbf{t}=5\mathbf{s}$, during which the rotational speed increases uniformly.

1. Determine the average increase in the rotational speed of the spin dryer per second, $\boldsymbol{\mathrm{b}}$.
2. Calculate the total number of revolutions, $\mathfrak{q}$, the drum completes.

ready2_open_rewrite.resolved_question_text: A washing machine spin dryer rotates about a vertical axis. When operating at a steady state, its rotational speed is $\mathfrak{n}=600\mathrm{r/min}$ (i.e., 600 revolutions per minute). The spin dryer accelerates from rest to its steady-state rotational speed in a time interval of $\mathbf{t}=5\mathbf{s}$, during which the rotational speed increases uniformly. 1. Determine the average increase in the rotational speed of the spin dryer per second, $\boldsymbol{\mathrm{b}}$. 2. Calculate the total number of revolutions, $\mathfrak{q}$, the drum completes.
ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: First describe the image: In the figure is the cylindrical inner tub of a washing machine spin-drying tub; the tub wall has many small holes; at the center of the tub there is a vertical dashed line serving as the rotation axis; the curved arrow above indicates that the tub rotates around this vertical axis. Then reason: The problem gives the steady rotational speed n = 600 r/min, the acceleration time t = 5 s, and the rotational speed increases uniformly from rest. First convert units: 600 r/min = 600/60 = 10 r/s. The average increase in rotational speed per second is the change in rotational speed divided by time, namely b = (10 - 0)/5 = 2 r/s per second; according to the answer convention of the problem, it is written as 2 r/s. To find the total number of revolutions during the acceleration process, the area of the rotational-speed-time graph can be used; since the rotational speed uniformly increases from 0 to 10 r/s, the average rotational speed is (0 + 10)/2 = 5 r/s, so q = 5 × 5 = 25 r.
